title: Later rapid gain and full wind recovery gave different labels in 12 of 86 Atlantic storms with complete 72-hour records, 1982-2025
abstract: We tested whether later rapid intensification (RI) identifies full return to a prior wind peak after a first loss of at least 20 kt following RI. We used Atlantic HURDAT2 release 092326 for 1982-2025. There were 188 first-loss origins. Only 86 had complete tropical records for the next 72 hours. In these 86, eight storms returned without later RI and four had RI without full return. Four had both labels and 70 had neither. Label disagreement was 14.0%, with a conditional 95% three-season block interval of 6.0% to 22.9%. Both forms of disagreement remained under all five planned rule changes. Across all origins, recovery was observed in 14, absent in 74 and unknown in 100. Thus full-cohort recovery rates remain unresolved. This is a rate-versus-level label audit, not a physical recovery mechanism or a forecast test. Heavy censoring, uncertain winds, land exposure, fixed rules and one basin limit use. Code, aggregate evidence, source hashes, a figure and independent primary-case checks support reproduction.
